subject: Geo activation / SKU tethering request for SapphireAI (US/EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SapphireAI committed capacity ask — tri-region (initial projection)

Hi team,

Quick summary from my call with SapphireAI this morning — they're planning a paid pilot with a target go-live in mid-November and want a committed dedicated footprint across US, EU, and APAC so they can meet latency and compliance requirements. High-level asks:

- Expected steady-state: ~120 concurrent persistent sessions (chat-style) translating to ~18K tokens/minute sustained.
- Peak allowance: short bursts up to 6x sustained for marketing/demo spikes.
- Data residency: EU requests EU-only processing for EU customers; APAC needs Singapore/Seoul locality.
- Elasticity: want predictable reserved capacity with burst lanes for marketing peaks.

They asked for a strawman sku split & month-1 activation plan and asked procurement to get pricing/terms. Attaching the usage projection they shared.

Can you sketch sizing options (conservative / balanced / cost-optimized) and call out which GPU families we'd recommend per region? Also need an ops checklist (SOW + provisioning timeline) they can put into procurement.

Thanks — cc'ing Kimberly who will drive internal approvals.

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: Sapphire_MLP_usage_projection.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SapphireAI committed capacity ask — tri-region (initial projection)

Thanks Ben — good summary.

I've read the projection. My initial thinking (strawman) below — please treat these as discussion points:

- Conservative: US 40% / EU 35% / APAC 25% (reserve capacity to cover 99th percentile sustained + 2x burst buffer). Recommend H100 class for US/EU for best latency/throughput; APAC could start on A100/4:4 mixes to reduce cost with a plan to migrate to H100 in Q2 next year if utilization justifies.
- Balanced: US 45% / EU 30% / APAC 25% with small reserved burst pool shared across regions (latency-aware routing).
- Cost-optimized: consolidate APAC to single micro-region (Singapore) using mixed-precision quantized runtimes and aggressive KV caching — target 20% cost reduction at the expense of slightly longer APAC tails.

Operational asks for procurement: committed node counts (by GPU SKU), lead time per region, SLOs for provisioning (we can hit week-of activation for US/EU if we prioritize).

Two quick questions for Karthik/Infra:
1) Can we present a model mapping tokens/min -> sustained GPU count per model variant (they plan to use a 70B LLM, 2x KV cache hit expected)?
2) What are concrete lead times for reserving H100 capacity in EU (Frankfurt) vs Seoul?

I'll draft the SOW language after we align on SKU counts.

Kimberly Park
Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_sku_split_v1.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SapphireAI committed capacity ask — tri-region (initial projection)

Kimberly, Ben —

Thanks for the detail. A few notes from capacity planning (quick, high-level):

- Tokens -> GPU: For the 70B model with our optimized runtime and expected 2x cache hit, ballpark sustained footprint is ~0.9 H100 per 3k tokens/min under steady chat-style concurrency; bursts factor depends on acceptable latencies (0.2s vs 0.5s tail). I'll attach a quick CSV model with parameterized columns.
- Lead times: US (Ashburn/US-East) H100: ~3-4 weeks for reserved commit; EU (Frankfurt) H100: ~6-8 weeks currently due to demand; APAC (Singapore/Seoul) A100 pools: ~4-6 weeks. If they insist on H100 in APAC, add 8+ weeks and premium.
- Burst lanes: we can carve a small global burst pool but it will consume capacity headroom in the committed pool — recommend a dedicated 15% burst reservation rather than fully shared to avoid contention for multi-region launches.
- Cost delta: H100 baseline is ~1.6-1.9x A100 for the same throughput depending on kernel selection and quantization.

Action items for sizing doc:
- I will produce three concrete SKU tables (conservative / balanced / cost-opt) with node counts, expected tokens/min coverage, and expected provisioning lead times.
- Need Sapphire traffic split by geography (Ben — can you confirm %) and their runway for committed months (3/6/12).

Attachment: capacity_model_v2.csv (csv, 18KB)

--
Karthik Iyer
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice@sapphire.ai>, procurement@sapphire.ai
Date: 2026-09-05T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SapphireAI committed capacity ask — tri-region (initial projection)

Following up with answers from the customer call:

- Geography split (expected month 1): US 50% / EU 30% / APAC 20%. They said EU traffic will grow faster month-to-month (expected to cross 40% within 3 months).
- Commitment horizon: they are comfortable with a 6-month reserved commit for pilot; if performance and unit economics look good, they will move to 12-months for production.
- APAC locality: primary ask is Singapore; Seoul is a secondary preference only if latency targets aren't met.
- Procurement contact: Alice Chen (alice@sapphire.ai) — she'll lead SOW and PO.

Alice — looping you in to confirm procurement timelines and what level of contract language you need around data residency & logging.

--
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice@sapphire.ai>, procurement@sapphire.ai
Date: 2026-09-06T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SapphireAI committed capacity ask — tri-region (initial projection)

Thanks all — based on the updated split and Karthik's lead times, here's what I propose we send as the internal ask to Infra/Procurement to turn into a pricing + SOW draft:

- Tier: Balanced (preferred)
- Month-1 committed split (nodes approximate):
  - US (Ashburn): 6 x H100 nodes reserved (covers ~50% steady-state + 15% burst buffer)
  - EU (Frankfurt): 4 x H100 nodes reserved (covers ~30% steady-state + 15% burst buffer)
  - APAC (Singapore): 3 x A100 nodes reserved (covers ~20% steady-state + 10% burst buffer)

- Burst lanes: 2-node shared burst pool (region-affinitized) — we can convert this to regional burst if needed.
- Lead times & escalation: request EU H100 priority (Frankfurt, 6 weeks) and flag APAC H100 only if Sapphire upgrades commitment to 12 months.
- Ops items to include in SOW: provisioning timeline per region, SLA for activation, data residency clause for EU traffic, capacity rollback / credit terms for underutilization.

Please confirm that infra can actually guarantee the 6/4/3 node split and that procurement can generate a 6-month pricing schedule. I will draft the SOW skeleton and a one-page runbook for their procurement team once confirmed.

Next step: schedule a 30-min alignment call with Infra, CS, and Procurement — propose 2026-09-08 09:00 PT.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
